issues.description: Email validation regex is inadequate and can be bypassed. The pattern /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ is too permissive and fails on RFC-compliant email addresses.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a battle-tested library like zod or email-validator instead of custom regex. Consider: const emailSchema = z.string().email();

issues.description: XSS prevention through simple string replacement is insufficient. This approach is easily bypassed (case-sensitivity, encoded variations, attribute-based XSS not covered).
issues.suggestion: Use a proven sanitization library like DOMPurify or xss. Example: import DOMPurify from 'isomorphic-dompurify'; const sanitized = DOMPurify.sanitize(input);

issues.description: ID generation using Math.random() and simple concatenation is predictable and vulnerable to enumeration attacks. Violates OWASP recommendations.
issues.suggestion: Use cryptographically secure ID generation. Replace with: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; return randomUUID();

issues.description: No maximum length validation on input fields. Vulnerable to DoS attacks through extremely long inputs (name field could be 1MB).
issues.suggestion: Add length constraints to CreateUserInput interface and validate before processing. Example: const MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 255;

issues.description: Database query shown as parameterized, but no verification that actual database layer uses parameterized queries or prepared statements.
issues.suggestion: Verify database layer uses parameterized queries. Document the SQL injection protection strategy explicitly.

issues.description: Error messages may reveal information about system state (email existence). Can enable user enumeration attacks.
issues.suggestion: Use generic error messages: throw new Error('Account creation failed') instead of 'Email already registered'

issues.description: Multiple responsibilities in createUser function: validation, sanitization, ID generation, user object creation, and database persistence. Violates Single Responsibility Principle.
issues.suggestion: Extract into separate functions: validateUserInput(), buildUser(), sanitizeInput() with clear separation of concerns.

issues.description: No rate limiting mechanism. Vulnerable to brute force attacks on user creation endpoint.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting at the route/middleware level. Consider libraries like express-rate-limit.

issues.description: Insufficient documentation. JSDoc comments don't explain security considerations, validation rules, or error conditions.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive JSDoc with @security, @throws, @param annotations explaining validation and security properties.

issues.description: No configuration system for validation rules (max lengths, ID format, etc.). Hardcoded values scattered throughout.
issues.suggestion: Extract magic values to constants. Create a config object: const CONFIG = { EMAIL_MAX_LENGTH: 255, USER_ID_VERSION: 'v4' }

codeQuality.summary: The file contains multiple critical security vulnerabilities that must be addressed before production use. Email validation and XSS prevention use inadequate homegrown approaches instead of proven libraries. Weak ID generation is vulnerable to enumeration attacks. The code lacks proper separation of concerns and comprehensive error handling. No test coverage exists. While the overall structure is reasonable, security and maintainability improvements are essential.

testCoverage.summary: Complete lack of test coverage (0%). All 5 exported functions are untested. Critical gaps include security validation functions (email, sanitization), core business logic (createUser), and data persistence (saveUser). The file serves as a fixture for code quality evaluation and needs comprehensive tests covering normal cases, error handling, security validations, and edge cases. Minimum 48 test cases needed for adequate coverage.

suggestions.description: Extract validation logic from createUser into separate validateUserInput() function. Extract user object creation into buildUser() function. The createUser function currently combines validation, sanitization, ID generation, and database operations.
suggestions.benefits: Improved separation of concerns. Each function has a single responsibility. Validation logic is reusable in other contexts. Easier to test individual steps. Clearer code flow through composition.

suggestions.location: Email validation and input validation pattern (lines 22-40)
suggestions.description: Replace scattered validation functions with schema-based validation using Zod. This consolidates validation rules into a single schema that serves as both validator and type source.
suggestions.benefits: Single source of truth for validation rules. Automatic type inference. Better error messages. Eliminates regex maintenance burden. Schema can generate API documentation. Type-safe throughout pipeline.

suggestions.description: Replace weak Math.random()-based ID generation with cryptographically secure UUID generation. Current approach is predictable and vulnerable.
suggestions.benefits: Cryptographically secure ID generation. No collision risks. Prevents enumeration attacks. Industry standard. No dependency on Date.now(). Simpler, more maintainable code.

suggestions.description: Replace generic Error throws with custom error types that distinguish validation errors from database errors from duplicate user errors.
suggestions.benefits: Type-safe error handling. Callers can catch specific errors. Different errors map to appropriate HTTP status codes. Better error reporting and logging. Clearer error semantics.

suggestions.description: Replace manual XSS prevention with proven library. Current string replacement approach is insufficient.
suggestions.benefits: Proven XSS prevention library. Handles encoded variations. Protects against attribute-based XSS. No maintenance burden. Industry standard. More comprehensive protection.

suggestions.description: Separate internal domain models from API request/response models. Add response schema for JSON serialization.
suggestions.benefits: Clear API boundaries. Independent evolution of internal and external models. Type-safe conversions. Automatic validation at boundaries. Better documentation through schemas.

refactorings.summary: The file contains several significant refactoring opportunities focused on security, separation of concerns, and use of industry-standard libraries. Priority 1 items involve replacing custom validation/sanitization with proven libraries and extracting functions to follow Single Responsibility Principle. These changes will substantially improve security, maintainability, and testability. Priority 2 items involve better error handling and type separation. The suggested refactorings align with clean code principles and modern TypeScript practices.

recommendations.description: Replace custom email validation regex with proven library (zod, email-validator). Current regex pattern is inadequate and can be bypassed.
Replace manual XSS sanitization with proven library (DOMPurify, xss). Simple string replacement is insufficient and easily bypassed by case variations and encoded entities.
Replace weak ID generation (Math.random) with cryptographically secure UUID generation. Current approach is predictable and vulnerable to enumeration attacks.
Create comprehensive test suite with 48+ test cases. All 5 functions are currently untested (0% coverage). Critical tests needed for validation, sanitization, error handling, and edge cases.
Add maximum length validation for input fields. No length constraints allow DoS attacks through extremely long inputs.
Extract validation, sanitization, and user building logic into separate functions. Current createUser() violates Single Responsibility Principle.
Implement rate limiting for user creation endpoint. Currently vulnerable to brute force attacks.
Use generic error messages instead of revealing system state. Current errors can enable user enumeration attacks.
Add comprehensive JSDoc comments with @security, @throws, @param annotations explaining validation and security properties.
Replace scattered validation with schema-based validation using Zod. Consolidates rules into single source of truth.
